about: The speech-to-text stack of this tool, chosen per language. Change models here or pass your own file with --config. Every Hugging Face model is pinned to a commit (revision); GigaAM is pinned by the SHA-256 of its files.
checked: 2026-11-04 against the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard (English, 2026-11-02), Artificial Analysis AA-WER, a 300-recording Russian benchmark (TypeWhisper), a Russian meeting benchmark (Habr, 2026-10-17) and the model cards; 2026-11-27: the model cards of ai-sage/GigaAM-v4 and ai-sage/GigaAM-Multilingual-v2 (both released that day) and the GigaAM repository at gigaam 1.0.0
calibration: a 14:40 English studio call: 108 chunks split at speaker changes, 52 flagged with the differing words, the flags fell on the real errors; 4 speakers kept apart, including a voice-over; the context list echoed once on a music-only chunk (caught as echo); both models agreed on two wrong words, so agreement is not proof. Russian: on GigaAM's public samples --lang auto picked ru, GigaAM was exact where Qwen3-ASR made three errors, and on a 71 s sample the flags fell on the real error spots. 2026-11-27, Russian: GigaAM v3, v4 and Multilingual-v2 read the same 110 chunks of two Russian studio recordings (9 and 14 minutes). Nobody listened, so the measure is the share of words that differ from the Qwen3-ASR reading: v3 12.3 % and 14.1 %, v4 9.9 % and 11.0 %, Multilingual-v2 with the tag «ru» 9.2 % and 10.4 %, with «ru-en» 8.8 % and 10.7 %. Words the plain head heard and the formatted head left out: v4 15 and 14, Multilingual-v2 8 and 7, the same with a full-precision encoder. Latin words written: v4 5 and 10, Multilingual-v2 «ru» none, «ru-en» 17 and 32. An English sentence inside one of the recordings: v4 and Multilingual-v2 «ru-en» exact, «ru» empty, v3 noise
review_every: 3 months: re-read the leaderboards, update the models and their revisions here
languages_note: «name» is the language name Qwen3-ASR takes and answers with: only languages that have it take part in --lang auto. «gigaam_language» is the tag a multilingual GigaAM gets instead of the language code. A cross-check is set only where Qwen3-ASR is within about 3 WER points of GigaAM Multilingual-v2 on its card; elsewhere a second reading would flag nearly every chunk. Only en and ru were run on real recordings; the other 19 come from the model card

qwen3-asr.why: English primary: the most accurate open English model that fits a 16 GB GPU shared with After Effects (Open ASR average WER 6.14, second among open models); free-form context biasing. Russian cross-check: writes Latin terms in Latin and takes the context list

granite-speech.why: English cross-check: another architecture and training set (Open ASR 6.59, released 2026-10-20) with keyword biasing; where the two disagree, the chunk is flagged for listening

gigaam-multilingual.why: Russian primary and the primary of 19 more languages: 21 languages with the language given as a tag; on its card 2.30 % WER on Russian against Whisper large-v3's 4.81 % and Qwen3-ASR's 6.05 %, and the lowest WER of the open models on every one of its languages except English; closer to the cross-check than GigaAM-v4 and v3 on two studio recordings (see «calibration»); punctuation, casing and digits built in; 776M params, 1.7 GB of GPU memory at its peak. For Russian the tag is «ru-en»: English names inside Russian speech come out in Latin and an English sentence is read as English
gigaam-multilingual.weak: names are still written by ear: the context list reaches the text only through the cross-check. The formatted reading leaves a word out now and then (7-8 per recording of 9-14 minutes): the plain reading of every chunk is kept in transcript.json as «raw»

gigaam-v4.why: not used by default; for your own --config: Russian and English, 238M params, about 0.5 GB of GPU memory, a third of the size of Multilingual-v2 and nearly as close to the cross-check, but its formatted reading left out twice as many words and it writes fewer English names in Latin

gigaam.why: not used by default; the Russian primary of 0.1.0, kept for your own --config. Russian only, keeps the fillers; 240M params
gigaam.weak: English names and terms inside Russian speech come out phonetically in Cyrillic («Фигма», «афтер эффектс»): the context list fixes them only through the cross-check

nemotron-diarization.why: who spoke when, up to 8 speakers, open weights (2026-09-23), 100M params; lower DER than pyannote Community-1 in a 132-recording comparison (English 10.3 % vs 15.2 %, Russian 4.4 %)

not_used.whisper / faster-whisper: whisper-large-v3 is 41st on the Open ASR Leaderboard (2026-11) and behind GigaAM on Russian
not_used.nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30: the best open model (2026-10-28; speakers and context lists built in) but needs 32 GB of VRAM or more, or a community 2-bit GGUF that is tight on 16 GB; revisit when either changes
not_used.GigaAM multilingual (the first line, 202: superseded by Multilingual-v2, the Russian primary since 0.2.0
